pos.personaBrief: La Máquina aimed at possession (La Página Millonaria), played short passes and dominated 'abrumadoramente' (El Gráfico 2014); Muñoz: 'agarrar la pelota, tocarla'.

pro.personaBrief: Patient short-passing build-up from the defence (seven-pass Loustau goal, Juvenal), no hurry to score (Muñoz); Moreno dropped deep to feed the forwards.

est.personaBrief: Forwards constantly swapped positions ('todos suben, todos bajan'), Moreno and Pedernera dropped to form a 'cuadrado mágico', tight combination play; positions were nominal.

lar.personaBrief: Muñoz and Loustau were true wide extremos who 'oxygenated' the team, while the creative playmakers Pedernera, Moreno and Labruna operated centrally with combination play.

blo.personaBrief: No pressing evidence; the team outpassed opponents and attacked 'sin pruritos conservadores', with no sign of a deep block or of a systematic high press by the forwards.

mar.personaBrief: Yácono was the 'precursor de la marca personal' and specialist man-marker; the Argentine 2-3-5 of the 1940s defaulted to man-oriented marking.

pla.personaBrief: River played its own possession game against all opponents ('You play against La Máquina with the intention of winning'); Peucelle only moved players to exploit their strengths and never gave instructions.

res.personaBrief: Spectacle: 'fútbol de lujo', 'se divertían en el medio', attacking vocation, and an ethos of beauty and romanticism (La Nuestra), while still winning titles in 1941, 42, 45 and 47.

sis.personaBrief: Talent-driven: Peucelle 'never gave an indication', play came from the players; stars like Pedernera and Moreno roamed freely.

jog.personaBrief: A team of technical virtuosos (Moreno 'gran gambeteador', Loustau's gambeta, 'exquisitez técnica'); Pedernera the cerebral playmaker; physical duels were not the identity.

bas.personaBrief: Mixed: youth promotions (Rossi, Carrizo, Peucelle's youth work) alongside signings of established players (Giudice, Rodríguez); title-winning core of experienced stars.

lid.personaBrief: Low-authority coaches: Peucelle disliked the DT title and gave no instructions, and the star line shaped the team; discipline came from the board, not the coach.
